title: A measure wrapped in COALESCE ( ..., 0 ) is never BLANK, so SUMMARIZECOLUMNS keeps the groups with no data
query: EVALUATE SUMMARIZECOLUMNS ( Product[Color], "Amount", COALESCE ( [Sales Amount], 0 ) ) ORDER BY Product[Color]

source.quote: Then a report or a SUMMARIZECOLUMNS query shows all the combinations of the grouping columns, including the combinations without data.
source.supports: replacing BLANK with 0 keeps the rows SUMMARIZECOLUMNS would drop

derivation: Blue is rows 4, 6 = 80; Red rows 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 = 460; Green has no sales: [Sales Amount] is BLANK and COALESCE returns 0, so the Green row is not dropped.
notes: The type of [Amount] is left out: the arguments are a fixed decimal and an integer, and no source states the result type of COALESCE for that pair.
